read.sections.0.text.note: Real facts: wheel in Mesopotamia (Lưỡng Hà), Bi Sheng in China, metal type in Korea (Hàn Quốc), Gutenberg in Germany (Đức). 'khối đất sét nhỏ, mỗi khối có một chữ' for movable type blocks. '1400s' written as 'những năm 1400, tức là thế kỉ 15'. Check the history terms and that 'máy in' is right. | Review: English 'grain' became 'lúa' (rice). Meaning shift for Mesopotamia; L06/L10 use 'ngũ cốc'. Also: 'Bi Sheng' is kept in pinyin; Vietnamese textbooks say 'Tất Thăng'. 'Hàn Quốc' for medieval Korea is the modern state name; 'Triều Tiên' or 'Hàn Quốc' is a political choice for a native reviewer. 'tức là thế kỉ 15' was added to 'the 1400s' (accurate clarification, not in English). [Reviewer changed: chở lúa và hàng hóa nặng → chở ngũ cốc và hàng hóa nặng]
read.sections.0.text.source: An invention is a new tool, machine or way of doing something. About 5,500 years ago, people in Mesopotamia used wheels to shape clay pots. Later, people put wheels on carts to carry heavy loads of grain and goods, which made farming and trade easier. Printing is another example. About 1,000 years ago in China, a man named Bi Sheng made small clay blocks, each with one written sign. Printers could move the blocks around to print new pages. Later, printers in Korea used metal blocks. In the 1400s, Johannes Gutenberg built a printing press in Germany. Books became cheaper, so more people could read and share ideas.
read.sections.0.text.back: An invention is a tool, a machine or a new way of working. About 5,500 years ago, people in Mesopotamia used the wheel to shape clay jars. Later, people fitted wheels to carts to carry rice and heavy goods, which made farming and trade easier. Printing is another example. About 1,000 years ago in China, a person named Bi Sheng made small clay blocks, each with one character. Printers could rearrange the blocks to print new pages. Later, printers in Korea used metal blocks. In the 1400s, that is, the 15th century, Johannes Gutenberg built a printing press in Germany. Books became cheaper, so more people could read and share ideas.

read.sections.0.simpler.source: An invention is a new tool or way to do something. Long ago, people in what is now Iraq used wheels to make pots. Later, people put wheels on carts to carry heavy loads. Printing is another invention. In China, Bi Sheng made small clay blocks, each with one sign. Later, people in Korea made metal blocks. Then Gutenberg made a printing press in Germany. Books cost less, so more people could read.
read.sections.0.simpler.back: An invention is a new tool or a new way of working. A very long time ago, people in the region that is now Iraq used the wheel to shape clay jars. Later, people fitted wheels to carts to carry heavy things. Printing is another invention. In China, Bi Sheng made small clay blocks, each with one character. Later, Korean people made metal blocks. Then Gutenberg built a printing press in Germany. Books became cheaper, so more people could read.

read.sections.1.text.note: 'Ở Kenya, một dịch vụ bắt đầu từ năm 2007...' keeps the English general (no brand name). 'đèn đốt dầu hỏa' for kerosene lamps. Check these.
read.sections.1.text.source: Some newer inventions spread very quickly. Mobile phones let people call, send messages and find information. In Kenya, a service that started in 2007 lets people send small amounts of money by phone, even without a bank. Solar lamps are another example. During the day, sunlight charges a battery inside the lamp. At night, the lamp gives light without any power lines. Many families once used lamps that burned kerosene, which made smoke and had to be bought again and again. With a solar lamp, people can cook, read or study after dark. But an invention only helps people who have access to it.
read.sections.1.text.back: Some newer inventions spread very fast. Mobile phones let people make calls, send messages and look up information. In Kenya, a service that started in 2007 lets people send small amounts of money by phone, even without a bank. Solar lamps are another example. In the day, sunlight charges the battery inside the lamp. At night, the lamp gives light without needing an electric cable. Before, many families used kerosene lamps, a kind of lamp that makes smoke and has to be bought again and again. With solar lamps, people can cook, read or study after dark. But an invention only helps the people who can reach it.

read.sections.2.text.note: '80 đồng xu' for 80 tokens. 'Hãy hỏi ai có thể dùng nó, ai là người quyết định...' Check the final advice reads naturally. 'rào cản' for barrier follows KEY_TERMS.
read.sections.2.text.source: Look at the bicycle trial in Riverstone. Cycling to the market takes 12 minutes instead of 30, so it saves Amara 18 minutes. That is a real benefit. But a bicycle costs 80 tokens, which Hana cannot pay, and repairs need parts and skills. The steps on the direct route are a barrier, because riders must carry their bicycles up them. Some people cannot ride a bicycle, or do not want to. Inventions can also cause problems that no one planned. Cars made travel faster, but they also made the air dirty. So when you study an invention, ask who can use it, who decides and what would help more people.
read.sections.2.text.back: Look at the bicycle trial in Riverstone. Riding to the market takes 12 minutes instead of 30 minutes, so Amara saves 18 minutes. That is a real benefit. But one bicycle costs 80 coins, an amount Hana cannot pay, and repairs need spare parts and skills. The steps on the straight road are a barrier, because riders must carry the bicycle up. Some people do not know how to ride a bicycle, or do not want to. An invention can also cause problems that nobody planned. Cars made getting around faster, but also made the air dirtier. So when studying an invention, ask who can use it, who decides, and what would help more people.

write.example.source: The trial shows that cycling saves Amara 18 minutes on the direct route to the market. One benefit is that she has more time for other work. However, one barrier is the cost. A bicycle costs 80 tokens, so Hana cannot get one. The steps on the direct route are also a barrier. Before giving out more bicycles, I would test the longer route with no steps. I would also ask if people could share bicycles. This would help more people because more of them could use one safely.
write.example.back: The trial shows that riding a bicycle saves Amara 18 minutes on the straight road to the market. One benefit is that she has more time for other work. However, one barrier is cost. One bicycle costs 80 coins, so Hana cannot buy one. The steps on the straight road are also a barrier. Before giving out more bicycles, I would try the longer road with no steps. I would also ask whether people could share bicycles. This would help more people because more people could use a bicycle safely.

watch.summary.note: Sensitive: slavery on cotton farms in the United States. 'máy tách hạt bông' for cotton gin; check the usual name. 'Hoa Kỳ' for the United States. The harm is stated briefly and factually, as in the English.
watch.summary.source: This video tells the story of the cotton gin, a machine invented in the United States in 1793. Cotton plants grow soft white fibre, which is used to make cloth. Before the machine, workers had to pull the seeds out of the cotton by hand, and this was very slow. The cotton gin did the job much faster. One worker could now do the work of about 10. Growing cotton began to earn much more money, and the cotton business grew fast. But the machine also had a terrible effect that no one planned. Cotton farms grew, and farm owners forced many more enslaved people to work on them. Slavery lasted longer. The video shows that one invention can bring both wealth and great harm.
watch.summary.back: This video tells the story of the cotton gin, a machine invented in the United States in 1793. The cotton plant gives soft white fibre, used to make cloth. Before this machine, people had to take the seeds out of the cotton by hand, which was very slow. The cotton gin did this work much faster. One worker could now do the amount of work of about 10 people. Growing cotton began to earn more money, and the cotton industry grew fast. But the machine also had a terrible consequence that nobody planned. Cotton farms expanded, and farm owners forced more people who had been taken as slaves to work there. Slavery lasted longer. The video shows that an invention can bring both wealth and great harm.
